groups.root_cause: The cache of rejected models is keyed so that it outlives a fix to the backend name, or deleting and recreating the model, for up to 24 hours.
The PATCH update logic gives no way to unset default effort, so the field can't be cleared.
Probe responses that arrive after a provider is disabled and re-enabled are not checked against the current generation, so an older response can overwrite newer discovery results.
At boot, loading runtime catalog entries throws a fatal error when an entry's name collides with a config model or its provider no longer exists, instead of skipping or reconciling the entry.
Smoke filters out providers that are disabled or missing without logging a skip or failing, so their checks silently disappear.
Smoke opens the live production database and applies the checkout's unshipped migrations before the release is accepted.
The test client decodes the :id parameter itself, so the tests never check that the server decodes encoded model names.
The escaped-process fixture depends on the child starting before the timeout fires, so a slow start triggers a retry and the test fails.
Eval eligibility doesn't apply the served-model guard, so models that discovery has confirmed are absent still get run.
